text:
jamie (AE): Hey team — NovusHealth procurement pinged: they want (1) an escrow/PO hold until countersign, (2) explicit KMS/HSM acceptance in the DPA, and (3) an SLA-credit formula in the order form. They also prefer net60. Can Legal + Finance weigh in on what we can accept and how to route signers? /cc @taylor (Sales Ops)

taylor (Sales Ops): We can enforce signer order in DocuSign: finance -> legal -> exec. If they insist on a PO before e-sign, we usually mark PO as "subject to countersign" rather than treating it as a binding trigger. Is procurement insisting that we not provision until PO is received? :thinking_face:

olga (Legal): Quick summary: we shouldn't accept an escrow that blocks our ability to terminate or provision unreasonably. We can add 'PO subject to countersign' language and an annex for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) with a supported-clouds list. For SLA credits, our standard is service credits only, credited to future invoices, with a cap. Example draft clause I propose below — will refine with their redlines.

```
SLA Credits: If Redwood fails to meet the Service Level Agreement for a given calendar month, Customer may request service credits equal to 5% of the monthly fees for each 24-hour period of unavailability, up to a maximum credit equal to 25% of the monthly fees. Service credits shall be Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for such failure and shall be applied against future invoices.```
Note: percentages negotiable, but we should cap credits (Finance will want a hard cap). Also avoid language that makes credits a refund or cash payable.

vijay (Finance): Net60 is fine for enterprise deals but we need a billing hold policy: require a credit check and a PO reference on invoices. SLA credits should be accounted as credit memos applied to future invoices; if credits exceed balance, issue a credit memo. If they want credits to reduce historical unpaid balances, escalate.

karen (Customer Success): From a POC/ops angle — we can provision a limited dedicated eval while redlines are in flight if we get an LOI or written confirmation that they accept evaluation terms. That prevents them from blocking the POC by withholding a PO.

jamie (AE): Helpful. Two asks: @olga can you drop a redline including the KMS annex and the SLA text above (I can tweak %)? @taylor can you confirm DocuSign template options and whether SalesOps can attach the PO and require signer order? Also confirm whether we can mark PO as "subject to countersign" in our order form header.

olga (Legal): Will draft and post a redline in ~2 hours. Proposed order-form header language: "This Purchase Order is subject to the terms of the Master Services Agreement and is binding only upon countersignature by an authorized Redwood signatory." I'll add the KMS annex placeholder and the SLA credits snippet above.

 taylor (Sales Ops): Confirmed — DocuSign supports required signer sequence and attachments. I can create an envelope template with signer order and include the PO as an attachment and a required checkbox for "I confirm PO is correct." I'll prep the template and share the link. :white_check_mark:

vijay (Finance): Credits applied to future invoices is our preferred remedy. Net60 OK after credit check. If they need earlier provisioning, we'll accept LOI + authorization to invoice later.

jamie (AE): Great — I'll ask NovusHealth to sign a brief LOI so we can start the POC while legal finishes redlines. I'll loop them on the "PO subject to countersign" language and ask procurement to confirm finance signer ordering. Will update with customer response. Thanks everyone! :pray:
